html:
Tegucigalpa is the capital of Honduras, founded as a Spanish silver-mining settlement in 1578 in the central highlands. It became the capital in 1880.

Silver and gold from the hills made it richer than the old capital, Comayagua. Liberal presidents of the late 1800s, who favoured mining companies, moved the government there. The Rosario mining company, run by Americans, was for years one of the largest businesses in the country.

Tegucigalpa grew slowly on its steep hills and never had a railway. It joined with Comayagüela across the river into one capital district. Its airport, among the most difficult in the world, was the gateway to the capital until a new one opened at Palmerola in 2021. Francisco Morazán was born there, and the city has been the political centre of Honduras ever since.
sum: Tegucigalpa is the capital of Honduras, founded as a Spanish silver-mining settlement in 1578 in the central highlands. It became the capital in 1880.
